title: Determination 45/1/239: egress windows onto land outside occupant control in a listed-building conversion (Requirement B1)
jurisdiction: England (UK): Secretary of State determination / appeal / tribunal under the Building Act 1984 and Building Regulations; comparative test only, not Alberta
code_edition: Building Regulations 2000 (as amended): Requirement B1 (means of warning and escape)

facts.text: The building work changes the use of a Grade II listed building from an arts centre into a dwelling.
The egress windows are in a wall forming the legal boundary of the property and adjoin an enclosed courtyard garden of an adjoining Grade II listed cottage.
The full plans application was rejected by the Council on 23 January 2009 because the egress window proposals did not comply with Requirement B1.
The Council's position is that it is inappropriate to accept egress windows leading to an area outside the ownership or control of the occupiers.
The Council identified alternative design options, including a connecting door between the two first-floor bedrooms, for which the land question would not arise.
The Secretary of State concludes that the unusual context of the two buildings and their listed status bears on the likelihood of further development that would prevent use of the egress windows.
Determination: the plans comply with Requirement B1.
